text:
Vance defended Trump's decision to launch the Iran war(Image: AFP via Getty Images)

JD Vance has declared he is "genuinely still angry at George W. Bush" as he accused the former president of betraying the trust of patriotic Americans through the Iraq war, while simultaneously defending Donald Trump's military campaign in Iran.

"I'm genuinely still angry at George W. Bush over this," Vance stated during an episode of the Diary of a CEO podcast released on Thursday. Vance reflected on how, during his high school years, there existed a "patriotic sense" that the Iraq war represented his generation's World War II.

"Even some of the historical analogies that got used were the exact same, Saddam Hussein was Adolf Hitler...and they were so good at tapping into that patriotic reservoir," he recalled. The vice president went on to express his lingering frustration at Bush for failing to be "careful" with that "patriotic reservoir.

"To have a real nation, you have to have the willingness that if, god forbid, something happens, you're willing to put on your uniform and go and do what needs to be done. But again, in order for that to work, in order for that feeling to be justified, leaders have to not take advantage of it. You can't say Saddam Hussein is Adolf Hitler. He wasn't. You've got to be careful with it. And I don't think that George W. Bush was careful with it," he explained.

Vance said he's 'still angry' at George W. Bush(Image: Getty Images)

Vance continued by stating that the Iraq war was not in America's best interest and "something that we shouldn't have been doing in the first place."

He stressed that leaders must exercise caution in how they characterize what they're requesting their young people to undertake.

"If you ask somebody to do something and it turns out you were lying to them, whether it was intentional or not, I think you draw down that patriotic reservoir," he said.

The initial invasion phase of the Iraq war was anticipated to last merely weeks or months, yet the conflict extended nearly nine years and led to the deaths of almost 5,000 US service members.

When questioned about Trump's war in Iran and whether it represents another "forever war", Vance offered a contrasting perspective. "Well the answer is no," he responded.

"When I talked about this conflict I always said Donald Trump learned the lessons, it's actually that's almost unfair to him, he didn't learn the lessons of the Iraq war because back during the Iraq war he was saying, 'This was stupid, we should get out of Iraq,'" Vance added.

"Now, obviously I'm an insider, I saw the president's deliberations and thoughts on this, but I never had any worry that this would become a multi-year expedition with no end in sight because I knew that we had a leadership that was trying to define the objective very narrowly, accomplish the objective, and then see where we are," he explained. Trump initially predicted that his war in Iran would last just four to five weeks.

However, the conflict is now nearing the four-month mark, and despite a recent ceasefire agreement being reached, a definitive resolution remains far from certain as tensions continue to run high.
